--- title: "Plotting trajectories" --- The columns of a `(B, 157)` array are fortnightly windows spanning six years of simulation. Plot against time relative to the campaign. That puts the campaign at zero and the response to its right. ## The setting The running example is a district with a measured under-5 prevalence of 0.45, pyrethroid resistance at 0.30, and pyrethroid-only nets at 70% coverage. The EIR comes from estiMINT, the net lethality from `calculate_dn0`. ::: {#c1093d29 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import pandas as pd from estimint import calculate_dn0, load_xgb_model, run_xgb_model current = calculate_dn0(0.30, py_only=0.70) setting = pd.DataFrame([{ "prev_y9": 0.45, "dn0_use": current.dn0, "Q0": 0.85, "phi_bednets": 0.80, "seasonal": 0.0, "itn_use": current.itn_use, "irs_use": 0.0, }]) eir = float(run_xgb_model(setting, load_xgb_model("prevalence"))[0]) print(f"dn0_use = {current.dn0:.3f}, itn_use = {current.itn_use}, eir = {eir:.2f}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` dn0_use = 0.311, itn_use = 0.7, eir = 31.96 ``` ::: ::: The three candidate campaigns below are all at 70% coverage and differ only in the net product. Each restates `itn_future`. Leaving it at zero would withdraw the nets. ::: {#5957aa01 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} from stateMINT.model import Mamba2Regressor prevalence = Mamba2Regressor.from_pretrained( "dide-ic/stateMINT", predictor="prevalence", revision="v1.2.2", ) cases = Mamba2Regressor.from_pretrained( "dide-ic/stateMINT", predictor="cases", revision="v1.2.2", ) base = { "eir": eir, "dn0_use": current.dn0, "Q0": 0.85, "phi_bednets": 0.80, "seasonal": 0, "routine": 0.0, "itn_use": 0.70, "irs_use": 0.0, "irs_future": 0.0, "lsm": 0.0, } products = { "pyrethroid-only": "py_only", "pyrethroid-PBO": "py_pbo", "pyrethroid-pyrrole": "py_pyrrole", } scenarios = [ dict(base, dn0_future=calculate_dn0(0.30, **{net: 0.70}).dn0, itn_future=0.70) for net in products.values() ] prev = prevalence.predict(scenarios) case = np.maximum(cases.predict(scenarios), 0.0) print(prev.shape, case.shape) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` (3, 157) (3, 157) ``` ::: ::: ## The time axis The axis is worth rebuilding from the checkpoint rather than from memory. The three numbers that define it sit in the preprocessing config. ::: {#83054f9c .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} cfg = prevalence.preprocessing_config abs_t = cfg["model_start_day"] + cfg["window_size"] * np.arange(cfg["n_steps"]) years = (abs_t - cfg["intervention_day"]) / 365 idx_y9 = int(np.argmin(np.abs(abs_t - cfg["intervention_day"]))) ``` ::: ## The figure ::: {#447627ca .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, (ax_p, ax_c) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(7.2, 6.4), sharex=True) for label, p, c in zip(products, prev, case): ax_p.plot(years, p, label=label) ax_c.plot(years, c, label=label) for ax in (ax_p, ax_c): ax.axvline(0, color="#8b93a3", ls="--", lw=1, alpha=0.7) ax_p.set_ylabel("Prevalence") ax_p.set_title("Parasite prevalence") ax_p.legend(loc="lower right") ax_c.set_ylabel("Cases per 14-day window") ax_c.set_xlabel("Years relative to the campaign") ax_c.set_title("Clinical cases") plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Prevalence and clinical cases under three net products, all at 70% coverage, in a district with pyrethroid resistance of 0.30. Blue is pyrethroid-only, green is PBO and amber is pyrrole. The dashed rule marks the campaign.](plotting_files/figure-html/cell-6-output-1.png){fig-alt='Two stacked panels sharing a time axis running from three years before the campaign to three years after. The upper panel shows prevalence, the lower panel clinical cases. The blue, green and amber curves coincide before the campaign and separate after it, with amber pyrrole lowest, then green PBO, then blue pyrethroid-only.'} ::: ::: ## Interpreting the figure The blue, green and amber curves lie on top of one another to the left of the dashed rule, and separate only to the right of it. This is because the campaign covariates are masked before day 3285, so scenarios that differ only in their campaign share an identical pre-campaign history. Note that curves separating before the rule mean something in the present has changed, most often `dn0_use`, `itn_use` or the EIR. Notice too that the shared baseline is not flat. `model_start_day` is day 2190 and the campaign is day 3285, one three-year mass-distribution cycle apart, so the window opens on the previous distribution and closes on the next. Prevalence falls through the first year as those nets take effect, then climbs for two more as they wear out and are not replaced, reaching the campaign at the top of the cycle. The saw-tooth repeats to the right of the rule. ::: {#d3a59070 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} pre = prev[:, :idx_y9 + 1] annual = {a: float(prev[0][(years >= a) & (years < a + 1)].mean()) for a in range(-3, 3)} print("prevalence given to estiMINT :", 0.45) print(f"emulator at the campaign : {prev[0, idx_y9]:.3f}") print() print(f"pre-campaign range : {pre.min():.3f} to {pre.max():.3f}") print(f"campaigns identical before 0 : {bool(np.allclose(pre[0], pre[1]) and np.allclose(pre[1], pre[2]))}") print() for a, mean in annual.items(): print(f"mean prevalence, year {a:+d} : {mean:.3f}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` prevalence given to estiMINT : 0.45 emulator at the campaign : 0.456 pre-campaign range : 0.288 to 0.491 campaigns identical before 0 : True mean prevalence, year -3 : 0.332 mean prevalence, year -2 : 0.369 mean prevalence, year -1 : 0.455 mean prevalence, year +0 : 0.339 mean prevalence, year +1 : 0.402 mean prevalence, year +2 : 0.490 ``` ::: ::: That output carries two checks. The three campaigns are identical before the rule, and at the campaign step the trajectory passes within a few thousandths of 0.45, the prevalence estiMINT was given. Run that round trip on every scenario. The agreement holds at `idx_y9` and not on average, because the annual means run from 0.33 to 0.46 and a scenario judged by its mean will look badly wrong when it is not. `prev_y9` is a point on the trajectory, and `idx_y9` is where to read it. A trajectory that misses the measured prevalence there means something is wrong upstream, most often in `dn0_use` or `itn_use`. Three years on the curves are ordered as the `dn0` table predicts, with amber pyrrole lowest, green PBO above it, and blue pyrethroid-only highest in both panels. This is because they differ only in `dn0_future`, and at 30% resistance the pyrrole net kills the largest share of the mosquitoes that touch it. The gaps are modest. ## A tidy frame Two arrays and an axis are enough for matplotlib. Anything else (a `ggplot`-shaped workflow, a `groupby`, a CSV for a collaborator) wants the data long, one row per scenario per timestep. ::: {#a1ae9522 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} tidy = pd.DataFrame({ "net": np.repeat(list(products), len(years)), "years": np.tile(years, len(products)), "abs_day": np.tile(abs_t, len(products)), "prevalence": prev.ravel().astype(float), "cases": case.ravel().astype(float), }) print(tidy.shape) tidy.head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` (471, 5) ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}
net years abs_day prevalence cases
0 pyrethroid-only -3.000000 2190 0.449371 2.086377
1 pyrethroid-only -2.961644 2204 0.450827 1.185663
2 pyrethroid-only -2.923288 2218 0.438303 0.658037
3 pyrethroid-only -2.884932 2232 0.415712 0.613480
4 pyrethroid-only -2.846575 2246 0.393178 0.564645
``` ::: ::: `prev.ravel()` flattens row by row, the order `np.repeat` lays the labels out in, so the result is three blocks of 157 rows. The `astype(float)` widens the emulator's `float32` output to double, which stops rounding from producing things like `274.299988`. From here `tidy.to_csv("trajectories.csv", index=False)` writes a file anyone can open in R, and a `groupby` totals the case burden of each campaign. ::: {#458e59fc .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} post = tidy[tidy["years"] >= 0] post.groupby("net", sort=False)["cases"].sum().round(1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ``` net pyrethroid-only 146.6 pyrethroid-PBO 125.6 pyrethroid-pyrrole 118.7 Name: cases, dtype: float64 ``` ::: ::: Filter to `years >= 0` before totalling anything. Summing over all 157 windows adds the same three baseline years to every product, and the absolute differences survive that, since the baseline is shared, but every total is inflated by the same constant, so cases averted and relative reduction both come out understated. ## See also Batching many of these into a single call is covered in [Performance and caching](performance.qmd). Please see [Trajectories and cases](../06-scenarios/comparing.qmd) for the same three-product comparison driven through the pipeline rather than assembled by hand.
